source.text: Daily (or higher) bias bullish and not invalidated; a complete bias statement naming the buy-side DOL, controlling range location, structural status, PO3 phase, time window, invalidation and conditioning event (ADV-M10-R01, P-BIAS-02).
Price in discount of the controlling dealing range, or has just raided SSL and is returning into discount (P-RANGE-01, ADV-M02-R01).
Expected kill zone supports the phase (manipulation complete, distribution active) (ADV-M08-R03).
Model permission: only long models eligible under bullish bias (ADV-M10-R07); Variation A authorised when displacement left a clean FVG/OB in discount and OTE aligns (ADV-M11-R02).
Eligibility checklist ADV-M11-R01 passes in full.
The kill zone the daily narrative assigned to distribution/continuation (typically London Open or New York Open); entries outside that window are skipped or need extra confluence (ADV-M16-R07).
SSL raid — the named origin pool (often relative equal lows or the session/Asian low) is swept (P-LIQ-02).
Bullish displacement + MSS (internal or external as required) (P-DISP-01, P-MSS-01/02, ADV-M04-R03).
FVG (and/or OB) forms in discount from that displacement (P-FVG-01, P-OB-01); array unmitigated.
Retracement begins toward the array (repricing inside an intact delivery leg, ADV-M06-R02).
FVG / Consequent Encroachment / OTE of the displacement leg (refinement hierarchy ADV-M16-R03: CE of a high-quality FVG inside an HTF array > unmitigated FVG/OB in discount > OTE overlapping FVG/OB).
LTF confirmation gate: liquidity event + displacement + MSS printed on the execution timeframe before entry (ADV-M16-R02); do not enter merely because price touched the array (ADV-M16-NT01).
Pre-entry checklist P-GATE-01 must pass.

triggers.compilation_note: The second trigger option is the pre-entry checklist gate; it adds no signal of its own, so it is compiled as the same confirmation entry with the checklist re-asserted.

source.text: Decisive close below the displacement origin, or below the far side of the entry array (P-STOP-01 B/C); alternatively beyond a recent LTF swing whose breach negates the internal MSS (D). Defined before entry; never widened (ADV-M16-R04).
First partial at the nearest significant IRL / intermediate pool in the DOL direction (predetermined fraction).
Runner to the named buy-side DOL (terminal); runner closed on target, on narrative invalidation, or by a structure-tied trailing rule (ADV-M16-R05, ADV-M16-R06).
Daily or weekly invalidation as defined in the bias statement — retires all long models until a new bias is constructed (ADV-M11-R03, ADV-M10-R05).

Bias is unclear when: higher-timeframe and intermediate narratives conflict without a clear corrective interpretation; no obvious DOL stands out; structure is transitional and no MSS has resolved the ambiguity; price sits at equilibrium of the controlling range with no displacement; a major scheduled event suspends the narrative. Response: stand aside. Unclear bias is not a licence to invent a direction. If bias is unclear, no directional model is authorised.

If a lower-timeframe range's premium/discount location conflicts with the controlling higher-timeframe range, require additional confluence or stand aside rather than entering long from deep premium (or short from deep discount) of the controlling range purely because a lower-timeframe signal appeared.

When the narrative or bias is invalidated: open positions that depended on the old narrative are closed or managed to the new invalidation; no new entries in the old direction are permitted; a new narrative and bias must be constructed before any opposing model is authorised. Continuing to trade a retired model is a process failure.
0.25-1% of equity, fixed

no_trade_dispositions.note: Bias, discount location and the raid-then-displacement chain are all required steps.
Lower-timeframe confirmation is the entry trigger; the session window is a gate; the engine never widens a stop and never adds to a loser.

Distribution models forbidden during accumulation or early manipulation; the engine holds one position at a time, so a long and a short model cannot run together. (already implied by this strategy's own steps)
The higher-timeframe bias gate is evaluated before any lower-timeframe setup can start.
Power-of-3 phase gate: no directional entries during accumulation, and the manipulation move is not traded as the trend. (already implied by this strategy's own steps)
'Re-check the liquidity and structural narrative' is a review instruction, not a market condition.
The setup sequence requires an array in the correct half aligned with the named draw; no array means no entry.
fvg_inverted requires a demonstrated hold after failure; the feature cannot label inversion at first trade-through.
Lower-timeframe premium/discount conflicting with the controlling range.
Overtrading is a behavioural failure, not a market condition.
Higher-timeframe bias no longer supports the traded direction.

source.text: When time-based expectations fail (expected kill zone produces no liquidity event and no displacement; expansion begins in a dead zone and is immediately reversed; a higher-timeframe opposing force overrides the daily time map), require a re-check of the liquidity and structural narrative, not a forced trade in the next window. Do not trade every kill zone regardless of whether a delivery narrative is active. Do not elevate a lower-timeframe signal appearing outside any relevant kill zone to the same quality as an in-window signal. Do not assume that if London did nothing, New York must reverse -- the higher-timeframe narrative still governs.

unsupported.explanation: 'Re-check the liquidity and structural narrative' is a review instruction, not a market condition.
unsupported.resolution: Record it in the run report; it is not evaluated by the engine.
unsupported.effect_if_unenforced: The run may include trades the specification would have stood aside from; reported selectivity is therefore an upper bound.

source.text: Overtrading = taking trades that fail the model-selection filters (Module 15) or the pre-entry checklist (Module 16), usually from feeling the need to be in the market -- includes trading outside the authorised session window, trading when bias is unclear, trading lower-quality arrays, and adding risk after the daily risk ceiling has been reached. When the model shortlist is empty, the correct action is zero trades. Revenge trading = attempting to recover a loss by immediately taking another trade not authorised by the narrative and filters, almost always accompanied by increased size or loosened invalidation -- after a loss, return to the narrative stack and selection procedure; if invalidated or no sequence appears, take no further risk (daily loss limit is the final backstop). Do not use fixed-pip stops that ignore the array and structure. Do not reject a high-quality narrative solely because R:R is below an arbitrary number. Do not widen the stop after entry 'to give it room.' Do not continue trading after the daily loss limit has been hit. Do not revenge-size the next trade after a loss. Do not treat 'I need to make back the loss' as a valid reason to select a model. Do not ignore narrative invalidation because the trade is still open and 'might come back.'
